translation_notes: the single np.assertion.add((URIRef, URIRef, Literal)) becomes one island: <http://test> <http://example.org/count> "not-a-number"^^xsd:integer -- the three term constructors and the tuple disappear, and the ill-typed literal is written exactly as it would be in Turtle, which is the point of the test

IMPORTANT negative finding (same as the NanopubClaim example): Nanopub.assertion is a READ-ONLY property and ldpy's only graph-mutation idiom is the augmented assignment `G += g{...}`, which needs an assignable target. The translation therefore has to write `np.assertion.__iadd__(g{...})`. A non-assigning mutation form (something like `G.add(g{...})`) is missing from the notation; here it costs the region its readability advantage.

context shim: `from nanopub_context import _minimal_valid_nanopub` replaces the same-module fixture helper (tests/test_nanopub.py lines 763-773 of commit 05022dc4bc), copied verbatim with its imports; identical for both sides. `from tests.conftest import ...` is not needed by this region.
pytest.raises / MalformedNanopubError / the ill_typed_literals list comprehension stay Python untouched; only the term-construction line changes
on the ldpy side URIRef, Literal and XSD become dead names in the rdflib import line, which is left untouched (the extract already carries many unused names from the source file's shared preamble)

demo harness added identically to both representations: the region returns nothing, so the harness wraps the fixture helper to capture the nanopub and republishes head/assertion/provenance at module level for isomorphism comparison; self is unused and passed as None
pubinfo is deliberately NOT republished: NanopubConf defaults to add_pubinfo_generated_time=True, so it carries a dct:created timestamp differing between the two executions
the driver puts the corpus checkout of commit 05022dc4bc (and the example directory) on sys.path; the whole region runs offline
